reason: E1 supports high Mn mobility and layered Mn/Cr oxide formation, but none of the cited evidence provides measured cation diffusivity values, a critical threshold, or a direct comparison of Al vs. Mn diffusivity effects on oxide protectiveness. The key premises about Al reducing diffusivity and the specific threshold are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mn in CrFeCoNiMn has high mobility and forms low-energy oxides, causing layered Mn/Cr oxides and pores
Cation diffusivity controls oxide scale growth and morphology in these alloys
Al substitution reduces effective cation diffusivity below a critical threshold (~10⁻¹⁵ m²/s)
Lower diffusivity with Al promotes contiguous, protective Al₂O₃/Cr₂O₃ scales
Higher diffusivity with Mn leads to porous, cracked, multi-layered oxides above 900 °C
